evals.prompt: I'm building a TypeScript CLI that submits brokerage orders. It already uses Bun but has no components.json. Add machine-readable output, a preview and approval gate, and an audit trail that survives a crash.
evals.expected_output: Inspects the project contract, registers @cligentic in package.json, views relevant live blocks, chooses and installs a justified closure, wires call sites, and verifies non-TTY and failure behavior.
expectations: Registers @cligentic with the package.json registry flow and explicitly preserves the absence of components.json.
Searches or views the live registry before choosing blocks rather than relying on a static catalog.
Selects JSON mode, trust gating, and crash-safe audit primitives with an adopt, hybrid, or reject reason.
Requires wiring call sites and observing non-TTY, refusal, and pending-before-side-effect audit behavior.

evals.prompt: Retrofit cligentic into this existing TypeScript CLI. Its published agent API must keep returning {ok, data, meta}; I mainly need safer config writes and standard errors. Give me the implementation plan before changing files.
evals.expected_output: Stops at an advisory decision table, preserves the published envelope, adopts or hybridizes compatible blocks, and rejects any conflicting output helper with a concrete reason.
expectations: Returns a plan without installing or changing project files.
Treats the published {ok, data, meta} envelope as higher priority than a conflicting shared block.
Evaluates config, atomic-write, and error-map from the live registry with explicit decisions.
Includes contract-focused verification and intended call-site checks.

evals.prompt: Add a reusable retry-budget primitive to the cligentic registry. It came from a production CLI and needs documentation, generated registry output, and proof that a clean consumer can install it without components.json.
evals.expected_output: Uses the authoring branch, extracts a generic block into the right layer, updates source, registry, docs and catalog, runs all distribution builds, and verifies an isolated package.json-only consumer.
expectations: Requires real provenance, a justified registry layer, and removal of project-specific details.
Accounts for registry source, registry.json, MDX documentation, README catalog, and generated site surfaces.
Runs the root build, site build, and package.json-only registry E2E.
Verifies a clean consumer with no components.json and checks generated JSON/raw source parity.
